still_open.title: The acceptance audit exits 0 when it measured nothing at all
still_open.why: The fix added `pageErrors` and `pagesFetched` and a header line claiming assertion 4 ("It actually measured something"), but neither value reaches the exit code: `const failed = missing.length + offenders.length` (line 226). If every article page returns non-200 — the Cloudflare bot challenge the new comment at line 136 names by name — or every fetch throws, `pagesFetched` is 0, `bodyCount` is 0, `missing` and `offenders` are empty, and the script prints `BODY IMAGE EXIT: 0` and exits 0. The only zero-measurement guard is still the pre-existing `pages.length === 0` sitemap check, which was already there in 1e28ddd. The fix also made one sub-case worse: a fetch that THREW previously propagated to `main().catch` and exited 1; it is now caught, pushed to the unread `pageErrors`, and the run continues to a green exit.

new_defects_introduced_by_fixes.title: `cropOffenders` is collected but never reported or counted, so documented assertion 3 (cover crops over CROP_CEILING) never fails the run
new_defects_introduced_by_fixes.description: The fix added `--crop-ceiling` (default 300,000 B), the `cropOffenders` array (line 124), the push at line 181, and a header promising "3. No cover crop is over `--crop-ceiling` … this is the only check that can tell a completed purge from a forgotten one" and "Exit 0 when all four hold". `cropOffenders` is then never read: it appears nowhere in the RESULT block and nowhere in `const failed = missing.length + offenders.length`. The header before the fix said the cover was "measured and reported but NOT failed on"; after the fix the code behaves the same way while the documentation asserts the opposite — worse than the honest previous state, because this audit is the only post-purge verification for the crops phase. A run against production with 309 unpurged 500 KB+ crops still at the edge prints EXIT 0 and never even lists them.
new_defects_introduced_by_fixes.fix: Include the crop offenders in the failure count and print them: `const failed = missing.length + offenders.length + cropOffenders.length;` plus an `if (cropOffenders.length > 0)` block that reports the distinct URLs by size, in the same shape as the existing `OVER CEILING` block.
